claim: Finding bugs purely by examining a changeset during code review is not generally possible and requires luck; the real function of code review is to identify code that will be hard to maintain.
stance_target: relying on code review (human or AI) as the primary bug-catching mechanism in a software factory QC pipeline
quoted_support: anyone who depends on code review to find bugs is living in a fool's paradise... Finding bugs, just from examining a change set, is extremely difficult and requires a certain amount of luck.

claim: A time-boxed review protocol (e.g. 'look at this for two hours, note what you don't understand, note where you stopped') gives reviewers a well-defined deliverable and signals when a change set is too large/complex and should be split.
stance_target: rigid evals / structured review SOPs for AI agent skill sequences
scope_conditions: proposed practice, not empirically validated at scale
quoted_support: Look at this for two hours, write a note about anything you don't understand, and if you don't get all the way through, make a note about where you stopped.

claim: Human review of diffs cannot detect runtime-state bugs like race conditions or values going negative under load; those require tests against real inputs, not review.
stance_target: separating automated correctness testing from maintainability-focused review in the factory's blast-radius containment design
quoted_support: A human skimming a diff cannot see a race condition or a discount that goes negative under load. Review is for code you will hate maintaining later; tests are for code that is broken now.

claim: As agentic coding tools proliferate, the engineering review role is shifting from inspecting code line-by-line to reviewing AI-generated reviews of code, and ultimately to validating architecture, intent, and business logic -- a shift that may itself eventually be automated.
stance_target: the software factory's director/worker agent hierarchy where human oversight moves up a level of abstraction
quoted_support: The role of the engineer continues to move further away from the actual code and toward validating architecture, intent and business logic. In the future, even that may be automated.

claim: Code review catches style, architecture, readability, and maintainability; tests catch bugs; production catches everything else -- best engineering organizations build automated correctness verification rather than relying on a human spotting an edge case in a pull request.
stance_target: layered QC architecture (automated test gates before any human/AI review) for an autonomous software factory
quoted_support: Code review catches style, architecture, readability and maintainability. Tests catch bugs. Production catches everything else. The best engineering organizations don't rely on another developer spotting a subtle edge case buried in hundreds of lines of code.
